text:
alex.p: Quick proposal — add an optional request header `Vector-Dimensionality` (int) and a server-side heuristic that suggests a client-side split when payloads contain mixed dimensional vectors or exceed byte thresholds. The goal: clearer failure modes + console suggestions for splits and cost estimates.

mira: Do you mean fail-fast on mixed dims or accept and split on our side? Mixed dims has historically been a nightmare for runtime. :grimacing:

alex.p: Prefer fail-fast by default but expose an opt-in header `X-AutoSplit: yes` that allows the platform to split and route. That keeps semantics explicit. Also want console to show an inline suggestion: "Split into N requests to reduce latency/cost" with estimated token/compute units.

samuel: Agree fail-fast is safer. If we do autosplit we need deterministic routing semantics so downstream billing/quotas are traceable per-origin request. Otherwise customers will be confused why a single API key got broken into multiple charge events.

mira: For telemetry, we should emit `embed_dim_histogram` + `embed_bytes_per_item` and a `split_decision` tag (none/auto/manual) so console can surface why we recommended splitting. Also track `split_success_latency_pct` and `split_error_rate`.

console-bot: suggestion: Add a console preview panel showing "Estimated calls after split", "Estimated latency P95", "Estimated cost delta" — can be computed from model cost profile + historical latency per batch size.

alex.p: Example header idea: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Vector-Dimensionality: 1024" -H "X-AutoSplit: yes" POST /v1/embeddings``` If missing, runtime infers dims from first item; if it finds mismatch, it returns 400 unless X-AutoSplit=yes.

tasha: How do we handle variable-length vectors from legacy clients submitting floats as different lengths? Do we want a migration window where we auto-coerce small mismatches (e.g., +/-1) or strict?

leo: My vote: conservative — strict mismatch -> 400. But for small delta (<=2 dims) we can provide a preview/console hint to the dev (not auto-coerce). Coercion often masks upstream bugs.

samuel: Quotas: split requests should be attributed back to the original request ID in billing logs. Add `orig_request_id` and `orig_vector_count` to each split call's envelope so we can roll up. Also add `split_frag_index` and `split_frag_count`.

mira: Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind `embed-payload-granularity`. Stage 1 (internal only) 100% -> collect telemetry. Stage 2 (canary) enable X-AutoSplit for 5% of orgs that opt-in via console toggle. Stage 3: public default = fail-fast, console opt-in for autosplit. Need dashboards: split rate, p95 latency, 413/400 rate, cost per embed call.

alex.p: UX copy for the console panel draft: "Your request contains vectors of differing dimensionality or large payloads. We recommend splitting into {N} requests for better batching and lower latency. Toggle Auto-split to let Redwood perform the split automatically; each split will be billed individually but linked to the original request for easier debugging." Thoughts?

leo: Add a small code sample in the UX showing how to implement client-side splitting with the JS SDK. Many customers will prefer client-side to avoid per-split billing surprises.

console-bot: action items generated: 1) telemetry schema: emit tags `embed_dim`, `embed_dim_histogram`, `split_decision`, `orig_request_id`. 2) API change PR: header parsing + 400 behavior. 3) Billing change: per-split attribution metadata. 4) Console: preview panel + opt-in toggle.

tasha: Also add a test matrix for mixed dimensional payloads (uniform, 1-off mismatch, random lengths) and large single-item byte payloads to validate 413 behavior and split heuristics.

samuel: We should also add a runtime guard that prevents autosplit when a single sub-request would exceed GPU memory budget for peak sequence length — emit `split_blocked_memlimit` telemetry and return 413 with guidance.

alex.p: OK — I'll open the design doc and PRs. For the immediate next step can someone own telemetry schema (mira) and billing attribution (samuel)?

mira: I can take telemetry. I'll sketch tags + example logs today.

samuel: I'll cover billing attribution and the request-envelope fields.

alex.p: Thanks — assigning to those owners. We'll reconvene after initial telemetry prototype. :thumbsup:
